item.source_question_text:
Which of the following statements is correct?
A. We can assume a "spherical cow" when analyzing the motion of a cow's leg. [incorrect]
B. We can safely assume a cow is a point mass when analyzing its position change in the scale of a mile over a certain time period. [correct]
C. We can never assume the cow is in a vacuum, even when we need to ignore the effect of air resistance. [incorrect]
D. None of the above is correct. [incorrect]
item.generated_question_text:
Which of the following statements about physical idealizations is most reasonable?
A. Treating a horse as a perfect sphere is appropriate when calculating the bending of its knee joint while running. [incorrect]
B. Treating a horse as a point mass is appropriate when estimating how far it travels across a multi-kilometer field over several minutes. [correct] Explanation: Over distances far larger than the animal’s size, the center-of-mass position change can be modeled well by a point mass.
C. It is invalid to model a situation as vacuum-like under any circumstances, even if drag forces are negligible. [incorrect]
D. None of the above is reasonable. [incorrect]
